title: A recent conference in Abuja, Nigeria, brought together African governments, international development organizations, and fisheries experts to address the pressing issue of food insecurity in Africa. Despite ongoing discussions, leaders from wealthier nations have failed to provide concrete solutions to the global economic crisis, which has exacerbated food prices and hunger, particularly in Africa. The rising costs of cereals, oils, and dairy products have pushed many into destitution, with some families resorting to eating clay biscuits in Haiti due to the inability to afford basic food items. The conference, sponsored by First Bank of Nigeria, aimed to raise awareness and encourage collaboration in the agricultural sector to tackle these challenges. Experts, including the president of the Nigerian Institute of Food Science and Technology, emphasized the need for increased production of staple foods like rice and maize to combat rising prices.
